 Get Ready For Clocks To Fall Back Beginning November 
 Posted by: Alexandra Ines 
 in Community News , Santa Clarita Latest News 
 October 18, 2026 - 3:25 pm 
 0 
 217 Views 
 Clocks are scheduled to fall back an hour on the first Sunday of November, resulting in the sun setting earlier in the day. 
 Coming up in two weeks, on Sunday, November 1, at 2 a.m., clocks will fall back, allowing residents an extra hour of sleep. 
 Daylight Saving Time (DST) was first proposed in the late 19th century by George Vernon Hudson, a scientist from New Zealand, and William Willett, a British builder. 
 In 1895, Hudson introduced his idea to the Wellington Philosophical Society. He suggested moving clocks forward by two hours in October and turning them back by two hours in March, according to Time and Date . 
 A decade later, in 1905, Willett independently developed a similar proposal. He recommended advancing clocks by 20 minutes on each of the four Sundays in April and moving them back by 20 minutes on each of the four Sundays in September. Under his plan, clocks would be adjusted eight times each year. 
 The first community to put Daylight Saving Time into practice was Port Arthur, Ontario, Canada, which is now part of Thunder Bay. On July 1, 1908, residents moved their clocks forward by one hour, marking the beginning of the world’s first Daylight Saving Time period. Other parts of Canada gradually adopted the practice in the years that followed. 
 However, Daylight Saving Time did not gain widespread international attention until 1916. According to Time and Date, Germany and its ally Austria became the first countries to implement the time change during World War I. On April 30, 1916, both countries moved their clocks forward by one hour to reduce the need for artificial lighting and conserve fuel for the war effort. 
 Within weeks, the United Kingdom, France, and several other countries adopted the same approach. After World War I ended, many countries returned to standard time. Daylight Saving Time did not become widely used across much of Europe again until World War II. 
 Today, more than 70 countries observe Daylight Saving Time, affecting over one billion people each year. However, the dates when clocks move forward and backward differ depending on the country. 
 Clocks will spring forward on March 14, 2027.

 About Alexandra Ines 
 Born and raised in the Santa Clarita Valley, Alexandra Ines has lived there since she was six months old. Her love for news and filmmaking started when she was young but was elevated with education. As a first step, she was accepted for the morning broadcast show, La Mesa Live, at La Mesa Junior High School. After her 2 years of exceptional work in the program, Alexandra was awarded the Outstanding Achievement in Video Production. She was quickly accepted into the prestigious Golden Valley Television (GVTV) at Golden Valley High School. In four years, Alexandra mastered numerous live broadcast skills, including crafting interviews and news segments. Most notably, she produced, filmed, and edited her very own baking show having a total of 12 episodes under her belt. In her junior year, she was given the mantle of the program’s producer, serving as a creative and informed leader for her team. Alexandra and a group of her peers created PSA videos on distracted driving and DUI awareness which lead to gaining 5 awards over 2 videos for the Streets Art SAFE Competition. Alexandra received her associate’s degree in filmmaking at College of the Canyons and is currently studying at California State University, Northridge as a film major with an emphasis in film editing. 
In Alexandra's role at KHTS, she edits news videos to serve as visual media for viewers. Alexandra spends her free time collecting and listening to her vinyl records and continues to bake outside of her baking show. She also enjoys travelling either by herself or with friends and occasionally going to live concerts.
